claim: No tested development family achieved the frozen joint feasibility requirements.
evidence: T02; Step7 and DB2 selection locks
boundary: Seven families and their finite grids; no assertion about every possible controller.

claim: Primary DB5 asymmetric fallback increased annotated-rest command exposure by 1.077 pp; stored 95% interval 0.764 to 1.397 pp.
boundary: Eight final participants; equal-person mean; requirement feasibility failed.

claim: DB2 transported and reselected fallbacks increased exposure by 4.165 and 2.572 pp respectively.
boundary: 32 final dataset IDs; same people in both contrasts; independent biological cohort not established.

claim: Active coverage can contain wrong active commands.
boundary: Coverage is nonzero held time; never label it accuracy or successful movement.

claim: Sensitivity effects depend on window/annotation/budget/decoder settings.
boundary: All 23 cases retained; no favorable case replaces primary; no multiplicity-adjusted new discovery claim.

claim: A novel controller or clinical benefit has been established.
boundary: Contribution is reproducible replay and constraint-aware evaluation, not algorithm novelty or clinical validation.

claim: Host profiling establishes hard realtime embedded control.
boundary: Finite measured host updates; no sensing/actuation, hardware-in-loop or worst-case proof.

claim: The proposed asymmetric method is better under all frozen constraints.
boundary: Development feasibility failed; do not use small descriptive p-values as proof of the constrained hypothesis.
